question.value: Spatially constrain the radial and vertical location, abundance, and ortho-to-para ratio of the c-C3H2 hydrocarbon layer in the TW Hya protoplanetary disk to improve the interpretation of the disk's C/O ratio.

evidence.quote: The present paper uses multi-line observations of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ to better spatially constrain the nature of the hydrocarbon layer in the TW Hya protoplanetary disk, with the goal of improving our interpretation of the C/O ratio(s) of this disk.

From this multi-line data set of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ rotational transitions spanning upper state energies from 29.1 K to 96.5 K, we aim to use excitation to constrain the location of the hydrocarbon layer in the TW Hya disk.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit observed radial intensity profiles with a grid of 1D non-LTE radiative transfer slab models

method.value: Run a 7,150-model grid of 1D non-LTE radiative transfer slab models (nLTErt1d) over radial annuli using the Cleeves et al. (2015) TW Hya physical structure, reconstruct 2D sky images, convolve with a 0.5'' Gaussian beam, extract radial profiles in matching annuli, and evaluate reduced chi^2.

evidence.quote: To fit the data, we use a simple slab model method (cite: Qi08; Oberg17) and employ a non-LTE line radiative transfer code based upon Ratran (cite: hogerheijde2000) designed to handle blended transitions and be computationally efficient (https://github.com/ryanaloomis/nLTErt1d).

To create the synthetic integrated radial intensity profile for each model, we reconstruct a 2D sky image of the velocity integrated line brightness and convolve the image with a Gaussian $0.5\ensuremath{''}$ beam.
Goodness of fit is assessed based on a reduced $\chi^2$ between the beam-convolved model spectrally integrated intensity profile and the data.

key_parameters.value: Min H2 column = 10^19 cm^-2; Max H2 column = (1 to 187.5) x 10^21 cm^-2; chi(c-C3H2) = (1 to 1000) x 10^-11 per H; OPR = 1, 3; R_inner = 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 au; R_outer = 80, 90, 100, 110, 120 au; Total models = 7150

assumptions.value: Physical structure from Cleeves et al. (2015) with disk mass 0.04 M_sun and 6.7x reduced small grains in the surface (1 A_V = 1.27 x 10^22 cm^-2 N_H2); constant c-C3H2 abundance within the slab; LAMDA collisional rates from Chandra & Kegel (2000)

evidence.quote: The gas temperature, dust temperature, and gas density are taken from this model, where the total mass of this TW Hya disk model is 0.04 $M_\odot$.

But since our model has 6.7$\times$ less small grains in the surface of the disk due to the formation and subsequent settling of larger grains, then $1~ A_{ V}$ occurs at $N_{\rm H_2} = 1.27\times10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.
We adopt the collisional rate coefficients hosted on the Leiden LAMDA database (cite: Schoier05) originally computed in (cite: chandra2000) for ortho and para separately.

fitting.value: Grid search over 7,150 models assessed via reduced chi^2 summed over annuli and all transitions equally, selecting the 30 lowest chi^2 models

evidence.quote: To estimate $\chi^2$, the flux in a given annulus for the data and model are measured per beam, and we sum the square of the difference divided by the observed RMS uncertainty.
To provide an even clearer picture of our best fit models, we extract the 30 models with the lowest $\chi^2$ from our grid and plot a histogram of the model parameters (see Figure 5).

validation.value: Tested +/- 10% flux scaling on the 4_{3,2}-3_{2,1} line and varying minimum H2 column between 10^19 and 10^20 cm^-2; neither changed the best-fit models

evidence.quote: We therefore have also examined our best fit models from the profiles as extracted directly from GOFISH, and then with a 10% uniform increase and decrease on just the $4_{3,2} - 3_{2,1}$, with the rest of the lines fixed. We do not find a change in the best fit models, in part since we have two other ortho lines.

Initially, we also varied the minimum column density of the layer, but since we did not see a significant change between changing the upper boundary from $N_{\rm H_2} = 1\times10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$ to $1\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$, we decided to fix the upper boundary for the full grid of simulations to the former value of $1\times10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$

evidence.quote: To test how much of the spread is due to the degeneracy between the thickness of the layer and the abundance, we also show in Figure 5 a histogram of the product of $\chi_{\rm c-C_3H_2}$ and $N_{\rm max}$ and find that this distribution is much tighter, and corresponds to an approximate column density of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ in the slab of $(1-3) \times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$.
We find $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ comes from a layer near the surface that extends no deeper than $z/r=0.25$.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: While this lower boundary does not directly correspond to a normalized height value of $z/r$ due to the nature of the assumed density profile (a power-law with an exponential taper), we can say that within the radial boundaries of the emission, that the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ arises above a $z/r$ value of approximately 0.25 based upon Figure 3, and no higher than 0.4.
Based on this sub-selection of models, an inner radius of 25 or 30 au is favored by 2/3 of the 30 models.

Nearly all of the best fit models have an outer radius of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ at $>100$ au, with 110 au favored slightly over 120 au.

findings_qualitative.value: c-C3H2 emission in TW Hya has a ring-like morphology bounded between R_inner = 25-30 au and R_outer = 110-120 au, and resides in the upper warm molecular layer at z/r between ~0.25 and 0.4 (extending down to A_V ~ 1-2).

evidence.quote: While this lower boundary does not directly correspond to a normalized height value of $z/r$ due to the nature of the assumed density profile (a power-law with an exponential taper), we can say that within the radial boundaries of the emission, that the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ arises above a $z/r$ value of approximately 0.25 based upon Figure 3, and no higher than 0.4.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: The inner edge of the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ distribution (25 – 30 au) is consistent with the CO snow line (cite: Qi13c; Zhang17) and/or the dip in CO emission (cite: Huang18) and scattered light (cite: debes2013; vanBoekel16).

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: The outer edge of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located at 110 – 120 au.

findings_qualitative.value: The rotational emission of c-C3H2 is thermalized (well approximated by LTE), indicating H2 gas densities > 10^6 cm^-3 at high altitudes (z/r > 0.25) between 25 and 110 au.

evidence.loc: The rotational emission of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ appears to be thermalized
evidence.quote: We conclude that the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ appears to be reasonably well approximated by LTE. The critical density for the transitions observed is typically around $10^6$ cm$^{-3}$, and our results suggest there remains a substantial amount of H$_2$ gas, $>10^6$ cm$^{-3}$, at high ($z/r > 0.25$) altitudes and moderately far out radii (25 – 110 au), consistent with disk mass estimates provided by HD for this source (cite: Bergin13; Favre13; Cleeves15; Trapman2019; Calahan20).

findings_qualitative.value: The abundance of c-C3H2 relative to C2H (~1-10% or 3-30%) is consistent with gas-phase chemical models with elevated C/O driven by volatile oxygen removal into large settling grains.

evidence.loc: The abundance of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ relative to C$_2$H is consistent with gas-phase chemical models
evidence.quote: Taking our best fit model abundances of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ and comparing it to the results of (cite: Bergin16) for C$_2$H in TW Hya, we find $c-$C$_3$H$_2$’s abundance is $\sim 3-30\%$ that of C$_2$H. If instead we use the column density, for (cite: Bergin16)’s C/O = 1 model, the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ to C$_2$H ratio is approximately 10%.

findings_qualitative.value: The ortho-to-para ratio of c-C3H2 is consistent with 3 across the emitting region.

evidence.quote: We find the ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is consistent with 3 throughout extent of the emission, and the total abundance of both $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ isomers is $(7.5-10)\times10^{-11}$ per H atom, or $1-10$% of the previously published $\rm C_2H$ abundance in the same source.

claims.hypothesis: Multi-line observations of c-C3H2 spanning E_u = 29 to 97 K can break excitation degeneracies and localize the vertical and radial extent of the hydrocarbon layer in the TW Hya disk.
claims.experiment: Extract azimuthally averaged radial intensity profiles using GOFISH for 7 transition sets (9 lines) of ortho and para c-C3H2 and fit them against a grid of 7,150 1D non-LTE radiative transfer slab models.
claims.result: Best-fit models have R_inner = 25-30 au, R_outer = 110-120 au, maximum H2 column density depth N_max = (2 +/- 0.5) x 10^22 cm^-2 (corresponding to A_V ~ 1 and z/r >= 0.25), and total abundance (7.5-10) x 10^-11 per H atom.
claims.finding: c-C3H2 resides in a ring between 25-30 au and 110-120 au in the upper warm molecular layer (z/r ~ 0.25-0.4) and does not originate from the deep midplane (N_H2 >= 10^23 cm^-2) or the tenuous uppermost surface (N_H2 <= 10^21 cm^-2).

evidence.quote: We can rule out $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ emitting from the upper surface (i.e., $N_{\rm H_2} \le 10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$) or from the midplane, below $N_{\rm H_2} \ge 10^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$.

The best fit models have similar characteristics, and abundance of $(7.5-10) \times 10^{-11}$ per H atom, and extend down to an H$_2$ column density of approximately $2\pm0.5 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: While this lower boundary does not directly correspond to a normalized height value of $z/r$ due to the nature of the assumed density profile (a power-law with an exponential taper), we can say that within the radial boundaries of the emission, that the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ arises above a $z/r$ value of approximately 0.25 based upon Figure 3, and no higher than 0.4.

claims.hypothesis: The ortho-to-para ratio of c-C3H2 in the TW Hya disk is consistent with the statistical weight ratio of 3 rather than a lower value such as 1.
claims.experiment: Include ortho-to-para ratios of 1 and 3 in the 7,150 non-LTE slab model grid and perform an independent disk-averaged rotational diagram analysis on the unblended optically thin ortho and para lines.
claims.result: All 30 best-fit slab models have OPR = 3 (no good fits with OPR = 1), and the rotational diagram yields an OPR of 3.02 +/- 0.78.
claims.finding: The ortho-to-para ratio of c-C3H2 is consistent with a constant value of 3 throughout the emission extent.

evidence.quote: There are no good fits that have an ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ of 1. Ortho-to-para of 3 is strongly favored over 1.

evidence.loc: The ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is consistent with a constant value of 3
evidence.quote: Figure 7 shows the results of the fitting, and we find that the ortho and para lines have consistent rotational temperatures, and the derived ortho-to-para ratio from the column densities is $3.02\pm0.78$.

claims.hypothesis: The c-C3H2 to C2H abundance ratio in TW Hya can be explained by gas-phase chemistry in an oxygen-depleted, high C/O surface layer.
claims.experiment: Compare the derived c-C3H2 abundance and column density in TW Hya with previously published C2H measurements in TW Hya (Bergin et al. 2016) and chemical models of oxygen depletion (Cleeves et al. 2018).
claims.result: The c-C3H2 abundance is ~3-30% of C2H (or ~10% in column density for the C/O = 1 model), matching the 1-10% ratio predicted by chemical models with volatile oxygen removal at z/r = 0.25-0.5.
claims.finding: The c-C3H2 to C2H ratio is consistent with gas-phase chemical routes in a high-C/O, water-poor disk surface without requiring additional carbon sources, though carbon grain/PAH destruction cannot be formally ruled out.

evidence.loc: The abundance of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ relative to C$_2$H is consistent with gas-phase chemical models
evidence.quote: Taking our best fit model abundances of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ and comparing it to the results of (cite: Bergin16) for C$_2$H in TW Hya, we find $c-$C$_3$H$_2$’s abundance is $\sim 3-30\%$ that of C$_2$H. If instead we use the column density, for (cite: Bergin16)’s C/O = 1 model, the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ to C$_2$H ratio is approximately 10%.

evidence.loc: The abundance of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ relative to C$_2$H is consistent with gas-phase chemical models
evidence.quote: In the $z/r$ layer of 0.25 – 0.5, that model finds a $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ to C$_2$H percentage of 1 – 10%, broadly consistent with our findings here, without the need for additional carbon sources.

evidence.loc: The abundance of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ relative to C$_2$H is consistent with gas-phase chemical models
evidence.quote: While the chemistry is consistent with gas phase routes, we cannot formally rule out carbon grain / PAH destruction as a source of additional carbon enhancement (cite: kastner2015; Bergin16; anderson2017; bosman2021).

why_this_data.value: Multi-line observations of ortho and para c-C3H2 spanning E_u = 29.1 K to 96.5 K probe a high critical density and a range of opacities, allowing excitation modeling to break the vertical location degeneracy inherent to face-on disks.

evidence.quote: The set of lines covers energies spanning 29.1 K to 96.5 K, and with the relatively highly critical density and range of opacities probed, these lines are well suited to constraining the nature, and crucially the location, of small hydrocarbon chemistry in TW Hya.

why_this_method.value: Used GOFISH deprojection and azimuthal stacking to boost SNR of faint para transitions; smoothed all lines to a common 0.5'' round beam for uniform comparison; parameterized vertical slab boundaries by H2 column density because hydrocarbon chemistry is driven by UV radiation; simulated blended ortho/para transitions via weighted population averages to properly account for optical depth.

evidence.loc: Images and Radial Integrated Flux Profiles
evidence.quote: We do not use these moment-0 maps for analysis, showing them here to illustrate the detection significance, and instead we apply the GOFISH package (cite: gofish) to improve the signal to noise of the radial profile for each transition.

The general reasoning for this vertical parameterization rather than a simple $z/r$ cut is that we expect the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ distribution to be driven by the stellar radiation field, largely UV (cite: Du15; Bergin16).

We took this approach since for some of the models the blended transitions became optically thick, so we could not simply sum the line fluxes from the independent components without potentially overestimating the blended line flux.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using moment-0 maps directly for radial analysis was rejected in favor of GOFISH azimuthal spectral stacking to improve SNR.

evidence.loc: Images and Radial Integrated Flux Profiles
evidence.quote: We do not use these moment-0 maps for analysis, showing them here to illustrate the detection significance, and instead we apply the GOFISH package (cite: gofish) to improve the signal to noise of the radial profile for each transition.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Summing independent line fluxes for the blended ortho/para transitions was rejected because the blends become optically thick in some models, which would overestimate the flux.

evidence.quote: We took this approach since for some of the models the blended transitions became optically thick, so we could not simply sum the line fluxes from the independent components without potentially overestimating the blended line flux.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Applying a 10% flux scaling to the 4_{3,2}-3_{2,1} line or varying the upper slab boundary between N_H2 = 10^19 and 10^20 cm^-2 were tested and not adopted for the final grid because they did not alter the best-fit results.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the models that fit the rest of the data give reasonable fits to the native $4_{3,2} - 3_{2,1}$ observations without flux scaling, and therefore we do not vary the flux for the remainder of the analysis described here.

Initially, we also varied the minimum column density of the layer, but since we did not see a significant change between changing the upper boundary from $N_{\rm H_2} = 1\times10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$ to $1\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$, we decided to fix the upper boundary for the full grid of simulations to the former value of $1\times10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$

limitations_admitted.value: The inner edge constraint (25-30 au) is close to the half-beam resolution (0.25'' = 15 au) and cannot be constrained further with existing data.

evidence.quote: An inner edge of 25 and 30 au tends to be a better fit for the $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ distribution. We note that this edge is close to the half-beam of the data (0.25$''$ = 15 au), and so cannot constrain this any further from existing data.

limitations_admitted.value: The inner and outer edge constraints depend on the assumption of a constant-abundance slab geometry; more complex structures would require higher SNR data.

evidence.quote: Finally, we note that both the value for the inner and outer edge only hold if a slab model is an adequate representation of the data, and certainly more complex structural representations could be explored with higher SNR data.

limitations_admitted.value: There is a degeneracy between the slab depth (N_max) and the c-C3H2 abundance because the emission is thermalized and fundamentally traces column density in a face-on disk.

evidence.quote: The flatness of the $\chi^2_{\rm reduced}$ for the best models suggests some degeneracy between the maximum column density, i.e., the depth of the layer, and the abundance of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ in the layer, which is to be expected especially if the emission is thermalized.

limitations_admitted.value: The upper boundary of the c-C3H2 layer is poorly constrained by the existing transitions.

evidence.loc: $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is located in and above the warm molecular layer in a ring
evidence.quote: We do not have strong constraints on the upper extent of the layer, and where additional observations for lines with higher upper state energies (and smaller Einstein A coefficients) would be helpful.

limitations_admitted.value: Due to data SNR, ortho-to-para ratios between 1 and 3 were not explored in the non-LTE slab grid.

evidence.quote: Ortho-to-para of 3 is strongly favored over 1. We do not try to fit between these values given the signal to noise of the data.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot distinguish whether the c-C3H2 OPR of 3 reflects an H2 OPR of 3 or a high ratio of electron dissociative recombination to ion-atom reactions (large phi).

evidence.loc: The ortho-to-para ratio of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ is consistent with a constant value of 3
evidence.quote: Therefore it is not clear whether our measured $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ ortho to para ratio is shedding light on the ortho-to-para ratio of H$_2$ or if it is related to the relative rate of dissociative recombination.

referee_caveats_inferred: The derived c-C3H2 abundance per H atom and the conversion from N_H2 to A_V and z/r depend directly on the fixed background disk model (total gas mass 0.04 M_sun, temperature structure, and 6.7x small dust depletion) adopted from Cleeves et al. (2015).
Spatial correlation between adjacent radial annuli that supersample the 0.5'' beam may affect the absolute scale of the reduced chi^2 metric if the full covariance matrix is not included.

evidence.quote: We present new observations of $c-$C$_3$H$_2$ taken as part of the TW Hya as a Chemical Rosetta Stone Program (PI: Cleeves, 2016.1.00311.S), augmented by archival observations from 2013.1.00198.S (PI: Bergin) and 2013.1.00114.S (PI: Öberg).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.0.00114.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.0.00198.S, and\ ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.0.00311.S.
